requirements.rationale: The operator chose (2026-11-08) one Hub-made notice over a second copy of the rules: the review already found the design's copied rule table disagreeing with the page on blocking questions, so a copy drifts.
requirements.statement: For every Hub event the in-app notifier treats today as ask, fail, done or reply (non-blocking questions included, as ask), the Hub SHALL publish exactly one notice on the operator stream carrying a stable notice id, its kind, project, agent, conversation when known, and the title and text the in-app toast shows; for every event it treats as silent, none. The in-app toast and any Windows notification for that event SHALL both be drawn from this notice.

requirements.rationale: Operator, 2026-11-08: the operator selects which events reach Windows. The Hub holds it because the closed-window case has no page to read it from.
requirements.statement: App settings SHALL let the operator turn each kind (question, failure, done, reply) on or off for Windows notifications, separately from the in-app switches. The defaults SHALL be question and failure on, done and reply off. The choice SHALL be held by the Hub, apply while no window is open, and survive a Hub restart.

requirements.rationale: The in-app toast, sound and flash are not seen from another app.
requirements.statement: While the app window is open but not the foreground window (minimized or covered), each notice of a kind switched on for Windows SHALL appear as one Windows notification within 5 seconds of the notice.

requirements.rationale: Closing to the background currently silences the app entirely.
requirements.statement: While no app window is open and a Hub this launcher started is running, the same notices SHALL appear as Windows notifications within 5 seconds, with no console window shown at any point.

requirements.rationale: The in-app toast covers a window in front; the hand-over between window and background watcher must not duplicate or drop.
requirements.statement: While the app window is the foreground window, no Windows notification SHALL appear. No notice SHALL produce more than one Windows notification, including across the moment the window closes or reopens.

requirements.rationale: An unnamed or 'Windows PowerShell' notification cannot be told from anything else.
requirements.statement: A Windows notification SHALL show AgentWeave's name and icon as its source, and say which agent or project needs the operator and why, in the words of the in-app toast.

requirements.rationale: A notification that opens the app in the wrong place is a second hunt. Operator, 2026-11-08 (option A): try real click activation first; if it proves impossible, the builder reports the criterion as not satisfiable and the operator decides, rather than shipping a click that only appears to work.
requirements.statement: Clicking a notification SHALL bring the single AgentWeave window to the front, restored if minimized, on the project and conversation of its notice (the project overview for a permission request or a notice with no conversation). With no window open it SHALL open one on the running Hub without restarting it, so running work continues.

requirements.rationale: Without it, a question's notice can reach no further than the project.
requirements.statement: The question_asked event SHALL carry the id of the conversation the question belongs to (null when it has none); consumers that ignore the extra field SHALL behave as before.

requirements.rationale: A notification is a convenience, never a dependency for work.
requirements.statement: When Windows cannot show a notification (notifications off, focus assist, the shell call failing, not Windows), the app MUST carry on as before: the in-app toast, sound and flash still happen, and no error reaches the operator or interrupts any run.

requirements.rationale: Thread lab, 2026-10-23: sounds by default for 'needs you' and 'stalled or failed'; 'done' is off by default.
requirements.statement: The app MUST play the brand's ask sound when an agent asks the operator a question or requests a permission, and the fail sound when a stall is recorded, a run fails, a message chain is suspended or a loop stops for any reason but a drained queue; a loop that drained its queue is done, which is silent unless the operator turns it on.
The app MUST show a toast naming the event's project and what happened, with an action that opens that project, and play the sound at a quiet level, when its window has focus.

requirements.rationale: Identity record §7: window in the background gets the sound, a count in the title and a flashing taskbar button.
requirements.statement: The app MUST, when its window does not have focus, play the sound at the normal level, prefix the title with the count of unseen notifications as '(n) AgentWeave', and in the native app window flash the taskbar button; the count and the flash MUST clear when the window regains focus.

requirements.rationale: 'One sound at most every few seconds; a burst is one sound and one grouped toast.'
requirements.statement: The app MUST play at most one notification sound per 4 seconds, and MUST group the events arriving within that window into one toast, the more urgent kind (fail over ask over done) choosing the sound.
The app MUST notify for events from every project on the Hub, not only the selected one, and label each with its project's name.

requirements.rationale: brand/sound/README.md: 'the operator can turn sound off'; the handoff asked that AGENTWEAVE_SOUND and the app setting agree.
requirements.statement: The operator MUST be able to turn notification sound off, set its volume and choose which kinds sound, in Settings, and the choice MUST survive a relaunch; turning sound off MUST also silence the opening sound of the native app, and AGENTWEAVE_SOUND=0 MUST still silence the opening whatever the setting says.

requirements.rationale: Spike 2026-10-23: a page's AudioContext in pywebview's WebView2 starts suspended, so an operator who opens the app and walks away would never hear the call this change exists for; --autoplay-policy=no-user-gesture-required makes it running.
requirements.statement: The native app window MUST let a notification sound play before the operator has interacted with the page; in a plain browser tab the sound MUST become available on the operator's first click or key press.

requirements.rationale: The first shipped opening came from a second synth that drifted out of tune; the brand keeps one source.
requirements.statement: The app MUST play its notification sounds from a copy of brand/sound/agentweave-sound.js that is byte-identical to it, and a test MUST fail when the two differ.
